# Wire fixtures — the bodies this server actually sends

`outbound-requests.json` is generated by `tests/e2e/wire-fixtures.test.ts` by driving the
**built** server (`dist/index.js`) over stdio against the mock upstream and recording every
outbound request verbatim. Field names and JSON types are the contract; the file is
committed so a change to either shows up as a reviewable diff instead of hiding behind a
mock that accepts anything.

Regenerate after an intentional contract change:

```bash
npm run build
UPDATE_WIRE_FIXTURES=1 npx vitest run tests/e2e/wire-fixtures.test.ts   # exits non-zero on purpose
git diff tests/fixtures/wire/                                          # review before committing
npx vitest run tests/e2e/wire-fixtures.test.ts                         # now it verifies
```

The regeneration run fails deliberately: a test that rewrites its own expectation and
reports green in the same run is not a test.

`idempotency_key` values are replaced with `<derived-string>` — they are derived from the
input or from a clock bucket, so the value is not the contract; its presence and type are.

## Why this exists

Twice (0.2.1 and 0.5.0) this server sent `mcc` as a JSON **number** while `apps/api`
decodes `MCC string`. Go's decoder rejected the body, so every sandbox policy call returned
HTTP 400 before the handler ran — and the test suite stayed green both times, because the
mock upstream is *this* side of the contract and cannot reject what this side sends.

These fixtures do not fix that on their own. What they do is make the wire bodies a
first-class, reviewable artifact, and make them replayable against the Go structs.

## Replaying them against the real Go structs (not yet wired)

The remaining half lives in `Shatale-SASU/shatale` and is deliberately **not** done here —
it is a cross-repo change. The shape it should take:

```go
// apps/api/api/v1/mcp_wire_contract_test.go
//
// Decodes the MCP server's captured wire bodies into the real request structs. A field
// the MCP renames or re-types fails here, in seconds, instead of failing as an HTTP 400
// in a published npm package.
func TestMCPWireFixturesDecode(t *testing.T) {
    // fixtures vendored from shatale-mcp-server/tests/fixtures/wire/outbound-requests.json
    for _, f := range fixtures {
        switch f.StructHint {
        case "apps/api/api/v1/sandbox.go sandboxAuthRequest":
            var req sandboxAuthRequest
            dec := json.NewDecoder(bytes.NewReader(f.Body))
            dec.DisallowUnknownFields() // an extra field is drift too
            require.NoError(t, dec.Decode(&req), f.Label)
            require.NotEmpty(t, req.MCC) // decoded into the STRING field, not silently zero
        // ...
        }
    }
}
```

`struct_hint` on each fixture names the Go struct to decode into. `DisallowUnknownFields`
matters: without it, a renamed field decodes "successfully" into a zero value and the test
certifies nothing — the same class of silent pass this whole ticket is about.

Until that test exists, the authoritative check is `npm run gate`
(`scripts/publish-gate.mjs`), which asks the real backend rather than guessing.
